model: PowerLogic HDPM6000 high-density power meter (BACnet IP)
applies_to: Schneider Electric (ex-Veris) PowerLogic HDPM6000 head units with busway, strip or retrofit measurement modules, on BACnet IP over Ethernet.
summary: The HDPM6000 head unit meters up to 192 branch channels, three-phase mains meters and circuits built from channels, and serves them on BACnet IP. Objects are grouped in numbered blocks: one object per channel, phase, circuit, TAP or harmonic. This list gives the first object of each block with its printed name pattern (e.g. 'Ch n Vrms') and the instance range. Analog Inputs hold readings; AV, PIV, BitString and CharString Values hold settings, alarm states and names.
notes: Each row is the first object (n = 1, or the first c, t or h) of a block; the description gives the variable range and the full instance range. Object k of a block is the first instance + (k - 1); harmonic blocks step over odd harmonics only, per the guide.
Names are the printed patterns; on the device n, c, t, p, v or h is replaced by the channel, circuit, TAP, port, value or harmonic number.

The guide prints some block starts wrongly: '3 phase meter 3 Ch n Demand Max Reactive Power' and '... Avg Current' as 17075 and 17078; by sequence they are 14075 and 14078 and are listed so. It also prints 13972-13984 for a 3-instance block (13972-13974) and overlapping ranges 1617-1689 / 1689-1760 for PIV channel alarm thresholds and warning delays.
Present_Value is writable for AV, PIV, BitString and CharString Value objects per the PICS, but the guide says configuration is normally done through Modbus or the web interface.
BitString Value objects (alarm and warning states, dry inputs) are listed as type Other. The environmental sensor block name prints '[3phm | TAP]'; shown here with a slash.
BACnet is only on Ethernet; the RS-485 port is Modbus RTU. Source: HDPM6000 Protocol Guide ZL0192-0G (04/2026), Section 4.

integration.summary: Enable BACnet in the head unit's protocol settings (web interface), then read the mains meter totals and the per-channel blocks you need, computing each channel's instance from the block start. Alarm and warning states are bitstrings.

minimum_points.name: Ch n Irms
minimum_points.why: Channel 1 RMS current; channel n = 119 + n

integration.enable: BACnet is enabled with a protocol flag in the head unit's network settings (web interface or Modbus); there is no BMS enable point.
setup: BACnet IP only, over the head unit's Ethernet port; no BACnet MS/TP.
Network, protocol enables and device settings are set in the web interface (see the head unit installation guide Z208128) or by Modbus.
No segmentation is claimed in the PICS.
gotchas: 'Ch n kWh resetting' (AI 600-719) is no longer supported and always reads 0; use 'Ch n kWh'.
Channel numbers above 120 use separate blocks (e.g. Ch n ITHD for 121-192); check the block's n range.
Some printed block starts are wrong in the guide (see notes); verify by reading the object names on site.
